title: Development and assessment of a machine learning tool for predicting emergency admission in Scotland
evidence: Derivation on ~4.8M Scottish residents' EHR (2013-18), cross-validation and temporal stability over 3 years vs SPARRAv3. The paper's own framing is future tense: a score 'that WILL BE deployed nationwide in Scotland'. Evaluation in this paper is entirely retrospective.

title: A deep learning based smartphone application for early detection of nasopharyngeal carcinoma using endoscopic images
evidence: Retrospective analysis of 39,340 endoscopic images from 3 centres. App accuracy 92.27% (90.66-93.61); NPC sensitivity 96.39%, specificity 99.91%, OUTPERFORMING NINE EXPERIENCED OTOLARYNGOLOGISTS - a standalone benchmark. Explainable AI highlights lesion areas. The app is built and distributable, and is intended to 'assist primary healthcare providers', but no clinician used it in the study and no live deployment was evaluated.

title: Interpretable machine learning model for digital lung cancer prescreening in Chinese populations with missing data
evidence: BOUND, a Bayesian network with uncertainty inference, developed on EHR from 905,194 individuals in China. AUC 0.866 internal; TIME-based external validation 0.848 and GEOGRAPHY-based external validation 0.841. Calibration curve with reported intercept and slope, decision curve analysis. A lung cancer risk scorecard was derived and made freely available online.

title: Multimodal AI for risk stratification in autism spectrum disorder: integrating voice and screening tools
evidence: 1242 children aged 18-48 months across a multicentre Korean network (multiple named IRBs). A mobile application collected parent-child interaction AUDIO and screening-tool data (MCHAT, SCQ-L, SRS). Two-stage model: Stage 1 AUROC 0.942, Stage 2 AUROC 0.914. Predicted risk categories agreed with gold-standard ADOS-2 (79.59% accuracy, r=0.830).

title: AI prediction model for endovascular treatment of vertebrobasilar occlusion with atrial fibrillation
evidence: Retrospective multicentre registry: 525 patients, data from 65 hospitals across 15 Chinese provinces, externally validated in a EUROPEAN cohort. 45.1% favourable 90-day outcome. AUC 0.719 internal / 0.684 external; calibration curves with max calibration error 0.088/0.091.

title: Real time machine learning prediction of next generation sequencing test results in live clinical settings
evidence: Model integrated into LIVE Epic EHR via DEPLOYR/FHIR APIs; prospective real-time predictions on Heme-STAMP orders placed in routine care (Jun 2022-Mar 2023), 3 ordering haematologists + 1 independent haematologist. Explicit aim: 'determine how accurately an automated ML model predicts... in real-time when integrated into a live EHR environment'.

title: GlioSurv: interpretable transformer for multimodal, individualized survival prediction in diffuse glioma
evidence: Retrospective analysis of 1,944 patients: internal cohort n=891 plus THREE external cohorts (n=84, 470, 499). Multimodal transformer on an accelerated failure time framework integrating multiparametric MRI, clinical and molecular variables and treatment data. IAUC 0.68-0.86; Integrated Brier Score 0.10-0.21; C-index 0.61-0.80. Sequential integration of imaging, then clinical, molecular and treatment data raised C-index 0.69 to 0.80 (p<0.001). Interpretability analyses recovered established prognostic factors.

title: Multi-cohort machine learning identifies predictors of cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease
evidence: Three independent PD cohorts: LuxPARK (Luxembourg, monocentric longitudinal), PPMI (multicentre international) and ICEBERG (French early-stage). Explainable AI models for classification and time-to-event analysis predicting PD-MCI and subjective cognitive decline within four years. Evaluated with cross-validation, DECISION CURVE and CALIBRATION analyses. Multi-cohort models showed greater performance STABILITY than single-cohort models while retaining competitive average performance; age at diagnosis and visuospatial ability were key predictors.

title: Deep multimodal fusion of patho-radiomic and clinical data for enhanced survival prediction for colorectal cancer patients
evidence: Multimodal DL (histopathology WSI + radiology + endoscopy + clinical) on TCGA-derived cohorts. C-index 0.82 for 5-year DFS; MSI AUC 0.91; AUCs 0.85/0.89/0.84/0.79/0.80 at 1-5 years. Comparisons are MODEL-VS-MODEL against DL baselines (PSF-SAM, NA-SegFormer, CNNs), not against clinicians.

title: Predicting opioid consumption after surgical discharge: a multinational derivation and validation study using a foundation model
evidence: TabPFN tabular foundation model (pre-trained on millions of synthetic datasets, retaining missing data). Trained and internally validated on an 80:20 split of the OPERAS cohort (n=4,267; general, orthopaedic, gynaecological, urological surgery); externally validated in a distinct general-surgery cohort (n=826). AUC 0.84 (0.81-0.88) internal, 0.77 (0.74-0.80) external; Brier 0.13 and 0.19. Patients with <50% predicted risk consumed a median of 0 oral morphine equivalents in week one.

title: Predictive modeling for step II therapy response in periodontitis - model development and validation
evidence: Development at LMU Munich with EXTERNAL validation at KU Leuven. ML models predicting change in periodontal probing depth after step II therapy from patient-, tooth- and site-level covariates. Calibration plots reported.

title: Deep learning on routine full-breast mammograms enhances lymph node metastasis prediction in early breast cancer
evidence: 1265 cN0 T1-T2 breast cancer patients RETROSPECTIVELY collected from three Swedish institutions. Adding full-breast mammograms to clinical variables improved ROC AUC 0.690 -> 0.774 in the independent test set. Good calibration; at sensitivity >=90% a significantly better net benefit and a sentinel lymph node biopsy reduction rate of 41.7% (13.0-62.6%).

title: Machine learning model for differentiating xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis and gallbladder cancer in multicenter largescale study
initial_category: D -> C -> B (resolved on full text)
evidence: Multicentre retrospective, 1246 patients (554 XGC, 692 GBC); AUC 0.94 internal, 0.88 external. COMPARED TO SIX RADIOLOGISTS: LIDGAX improved sensitivity by 1.2-8.5%, specificity 0.0-4.6%, balanced accuracy 1.8-6.6%, and reduced average diagnostic time per patient by 30.44-35.76 s. Deployed on an open-source online platform, maintaining AUC 0.95 / accuracy 0.92.

title: Interpretable deep learning for multicenter gastric cancer T staging from CT images
evidence: Retrospective multicentre study (1792 patients, two external cohorts). CRITICALLY: 'We additionally designed a comparative reader study in one external cohort to compare the model's performance against expert gastrointestinal radiologists.' Radiologists read WITH and WITHOUT AI: inter-reader Kappa for radiologists' sole interpretation 0.41-0.45, rising to 0.83-0.88 WHEN ASSISTED BY AI (p<0.001), i.e. AI assistance significantly reduced staging discrepancies.

title: Advancing diagnostic equity through artificial intelligence chest radiograph screening for osteoporosis in Asian populations
evidence: External validation of a previously validated commercial DL model in 2384 asymptomatic adults at Taiwanese health examinations, DXA reference. AUC 0.95 (0.93-0.99), sensitivity 79.7% (71.3-86.5). Decision curve analysis favours AI-based referral over refer-all/refer-none. No clinician comparison, no reader study, no prospective live use.

title: Multicenter validation and updating of the ELDER-ICU model for severity assessment in elderly critical illness
evidence: External validation across 12 international centres (US, Austria, South Korea, China) with three updating strategies (recalibration, incremental training, retraining). AUROC 0.804-0.864 in US/Austrian cohorts but 0.753 (South Korea) and 0.698 (China). Retraining improved AUROC by 0.066 and 0.076 at the two Asian sites. Isotonic regression and Platt scaling improved calibration globally.

title: External validation of a machine learning model for delivery mode prediction after induction
evidence: Portuguese tertiary centre (n=2,434) for development and internal validation; Consortium on Safe Labor (n=10,591) for external validation. Internal validation compared several ML approaches with an explicit aim of model SIMPLIFICATION; logistic regression performed best (AUROC 0.793, F1 0.748, PPV 0.752) and was selected. A simplified top-13-feature model was externally validated: AUROC 0.808, F1 0.781, PPV 0.822. Decision curve analysis showed good net benefit.

title: SurvivEHR: a competing risks, time-to-event foundation model for multiple long-term conditions from primary care electronic health records
evidence: Generative decoder-only transformer foundation model pre-trained on 7.6 billion coded events from 23 million patients in CPRD UK primary care, with a competing-risk time-to-next-event objective yielding calibrated cumulative incidence functions. Validation by PRACTICE-level split with test practices entirely held out. Benchmarked against traditional survival models and fine-tuned on downstream prognostic tasks. Retrospective throughout; no clinician used it.

title: Development and validation of a predictive model for extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
evidence: 977 subjects with extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma across 4 cohorts. Gradient Boosting Machine outperformed 15 other ML algorithms, yielding the ENKTL-ML score from 13 features (selected by importance ranking with backward-elimination sensitivity analysis). C-index 0.82 (0.76-0.87) in evaluation and 0.84 (0.81-0.88) and 0.83 (0.72-0.94) in the two external validation cohorts. Calibration curves, ROC and decision curve analysis reported. Stratified subjects into three groups with distinct survival; outperformed IPI, KPI, PINK-E and NRI (all p<0.001).

title: A Causal and interpretable machine learning framework for postcranioplasty risk prediction and surgical decision support
evidence: Multicentre (Qilu, Tangdu, Daping). Nine features, 15 algorithms compared, random forest best. AUROC 0.949 internal CV, 0.930 spatial/geographical external, 0.932 temporal external; lowest subgroup AUROC 0.927; calibration O/E 1.16 (0.97-1.40).

title: Interpretable machine learning models for stroke risk prediction in patients with newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation
evidence: Derivation cohort n=9,511 from National Taiwan University Hospital with external validation cohorts. Two models reported: logistic regression and Platt-calibrated XGBoost, using ONLY age, comorbidities and medication use to predict 1-year stroke risk after new AF diagnosis. Internal AUCs 0.915 and 0.914; external 0.877-0.886, significantly outperforming CHA2DS2-VASc (0.614-0.621, p<0.001). Calibration curves and decision curve analysis reported.

title: Predicting clinically significant prostate cancer with or without digital rectal exam and MRI data using ClarityDX Prostate models
evidence: Observational data aggregated from six organisations (Canada, USA, Czechia), biopsies 2009-2024. Calibrated random-forest ensembles derived (n=1626-2191) and validated (n=378-1318) at DIFFERENT clinical sites. ROC AUC >=0.80 (+DRE 0.82; +MRI 0.87-0.88). Entirely retrospective/observational; no clinician used the model, no prospective arm.

title: A transformer-based survival model for prediction of all-cause mortality in patients with heart failure: a multi-cohort study
evidence: CPRD Aurum: 403,534 HF patients across 1,418 English GP practices; practice-level split (1,063 derivation / 355 validation) giving geographic separation. External validation on 21,767 US hospital patients (MIMIC-IV) via transfer learning. C-index 0.845 (0.841-0.849) UK vs MAGGIC-EHR 0.728; 0.802 (0.789-0.816) USA. Calibration curves, decision curve analysis, explainability, subgroup fairness analyses. TRIPOD+AI cited.

title: Multicenter evaluation of interpretable AI for coronary artery disease diagnosis from PET biomarkers
evidence: Retrospective enrolment of 1,664 of 17,348 REFINE PET registry patients across 4 sites. XGBoost trained at one site (n=386), externally tested at three (n=1,278). AI AUC 0.83 (0.81-0.85) vs clinical score by experienced physicians 0.80 (0.77-0.82), p=0.02. Physician scores were made during ROUTINE CLINICAL REPORTING without the AI - a historical benchmark, not an assistance design.

title: External validation of the myocardial-ischaemic-injury-index machine learning algorithm for the early diagnosis of myocardial infarction: a multicentre cohort study
evidence: SECONDARY ANALYSIS of a multicentre international diagnostic cohort (12 centres, 5 European countries). 6,487 patients, 882 (13.6%) type 1 NSTEMI. AUC 0.961 (0.957-0.965); calibration intercept -0.09, slope 1.02. Compared directly with the ESC 0/1h-algorithm. Diagnoses centrally adjudicated by two independent cardiologists.

first_author: NIHR Global Health Research Unit on Global Surgery; STARSurg Collaborative.
title: A prognostic model for use before elective surgery to estimate the risk of postoperative pulmonary complications (GSU-Pulmonary Score): a development and validation study in three international cohorts
evidence: Derived in GlobalSurg-CovidSurg Week (86,231 patients, 1,158 hospitals, 114 countries); externally validated in CovidSurg-Cancer (30,492 patients, 726 hospitals, 75 countries) and RECON (6,789, 150 hospitals). AUROC 0.773 internal, 0.746 and 0.716 external. Deployed as an online web application. Intended to inform surgical consent, resource allocation and hospital-level prioritisation during pandemic recovery.

title: Development and external validation of a clinical prediction model for new-onset atrial fibrillation in intensive care: a multicentre, retrospective cohort study
evidence: Multicentre RETROSPECTIVE cohort, three UK and four US ICUs; 39,084 eligible patients admitted 2008-2019, of whom 2,797 (7.2%) developed new-onset AF within 7 days. METRIC-AF machine learning model with dynamic variables, final model 10 routinely collected variables; internal-external cross-validation during development plus external validation on multicentre UK ICU data. A simple three-predictor graphical tool and an online app were also produced. Non-linear association identified with hypomagnesaemia below 0.70 mmol/L.

title: Refined selection of individuals for preventive cardiovascular disease treatment with a transformer-based risk model
evidence: Open cohort of 3 million adults aged 25-84, CPRD Gold linked primary and secondary care EHR, England 1998-2015. GEOGRAPHIC split: 291 general practices for development, 98 separate practices for validation. TRisk = BEHRT transformer extended to a survival model. C-index 0.910 (0.906-0.913) in the general population; compared against QRISK3 and DeepSurv. Discrimination, calibration and decision curve analyses; stratified by age, sex and socioeconomic status; transfer-learned and validated in a diabetes cohort.

title: Leveraging artificial intelligence for predicting spontaneous closure of perimembranous ventricular septal defect in children: a multicentre, retrospective study in China
evidence: Multicentre RETROSPECTIVE study, 29,142 PMVSD patients across six tertiary Chinese centres. Dataset 1 (May 2004-Sep 2022, n=27,269) split 70/30 for training/validation; dataset 2 (Sep 2001-Dec 2009, n=1,873) used for testing. NLP extracted structured fields from raw echocardiography reports; 11 LASSO-selected predictors; random survival forest. Validation AUCs 0.95 at 1, 3 and 5 years; testing AUCs 0.95-0.97. Decision curve analysis, calibration index and risk stratification reported. Spontaneous closure in 3,520 (12.1%) at median 31 months.

title: Extension of the GRACE score for non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome: a development and validation study in ten countries
evidence: 609,063 NSTE-ACS patients from ten countries (2005-2024). 1-year mortality model developed in 400,054 (England/Wales/NI), externally validated in Sweden, Switzerland, Germany, Denmark, Spain, Netherlands, Czechia. In-hospital AUC 0.90 (0.89-0.91); 1-year time-dependent AUC 0.84 (0.82-0.86); well calibrated (slopes 1.06 and 1.09); decision curve analyses favourable. Individualised treatment-effect model externally validated in the Danish VERDICT trial.

title: AI-enabled forecasting of prehospital transfusion needs in patients with trauma: a multinational, registry-based, retrospective, machine learning development and validation study
evidence: Retrospective registry study. Trained on 364,350 patients from the American National Trauma Data Bank (2020); externally validated on 54,210 patients from three further registries - TraumaRegister DGU, National Office of Clinical Audit Major Trauma Audit, and Alberta Trauma Registry - covering Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Ireland and Canada (2007-2024). External AUROC 0.87 (0.86-0.87) for any transfusion and 0.88 (0.87-0.89) for packed red cells. Binary classifiers per blood product, a multiclass model for optimal combinations, and a regressor for PRBC volume.

title: Performance of Machine Learning Suicide Risk Models in an American Indian Population
evidence: Retrospective external validation of TWO existing published ML suicide-risk models (Mental Health Research Network; Vanderbilt) in 16,835 adults at an Indian Health Service unit, 2017-2021. AUROC 0.81 and 0.68 for 90-day suicide attempt vs 0.66 for a positive augmented screening indicator. Calibration poor for both models but improved after recalibration.

title: Development and Validation of a Risk Model to Predict Intraoperative Blood Transfusion
evidence: Development at Montefiore Medical Center (Jan 2016-Jun 2021); internal validation MMC (Jun 2021-Feb 2023); EXTERNAL validation at Beth Israel Deaconess (Jan 2008-Jun 2022). 816,618 adults; 2.3% received >=1 unit pRBC intraoperatively. Final model: 24 preoperative predictors; predictive accuracy comparable with machine learning models. Retrospective throughout; no clinician used the model.

title: Interoperable Models for Identifying Critically Ill Children at Risk of Neurologic Morbidity
evidence: Retrospective: 18,568 encounters (2010-2022) at the development site; 6,825 encounters (2018-2021) at an external quaternary PICU. Generalisable XGBoost, 24-h horizon: F1 0.37, AUROC 0.81 (0.78-0.83), number needed to alert 4; Brier 0.04 after recalibration. Predictions correlated with serum GFAP in a convenience cohort.

title: Validation of a Dynamic Risk Prediction Model Incorporating Prior Mammograms in a Diverse Population
evidence: External validation of an existing AI-generated mammogram risk score (previously validated in Black and White women) in 206,929 women aged 40-74 in the British Columbia Breast Screening Program (2013-2019), with outcome ascertainment by linkage to the BC Cancer Registry to June 2023. 5-year AUROC consistent across racial and ethnic groups; dynamic score using up to 4 years of prior mammograms outperformed a single time point.

title: Deep Learning Model of Primary Tumor and Metastatic Cervical Lymph Nodes From CT for Outcome Predictions in Oropharyngeal Cancer
evidence: Retrospective prognostic study, 811 patients with p16+ OPSCC from 3 independent cohorts, pretreatment CT. DL classifier integrating primary tumour and metastatic cervical lymph node features stratified patients into low- vs high-risk for disease-free survival, overall survival and locoregional failure. Calibration curves reported on the third cohort.

title: Predicting Agitation Events in the Emergency Department Through Artificial Intelligence
evidence: Retrospective cohort of 3,048,780 ED visits across 9 sites in one Northeast US health system (2015-2022). 50 predictors, AUROC 0.94 (0.93-0.94), PR-AUC 0.41. Outcome = intramuscular sedation and/or violent physical restraint order. No prospective arm, no clinician used the model.

title: International multicenter validation of AI-driven ultrasound detection of ovarian cancer
evidence: Explicitly an international multicenter RETROSPECTIVE study. 17,119 images / 3,652 patients / 20 centres / 8 countries, leave-one-centre-out CV. Model compared against 66 ultrasound examiners (33 specialists, median 17 years experience) who assessed independently - a standalone benchmark, not an assistance design. Triage benefit (63% reduction in expert referral) came from a RETROSPECTIVE TRIAGE SIMULATION, not live use.

title: Clinical implementation of an AI-based prediction model for decision support for patients undergoing colorectal cancer surgery
evidence: Model implemented as standard treatment at Zealand University Hospital from 1 Feb 2023; prospective clinical cohort n=194 (Feb-Dec 2023) risk-stratified by a consultant surgeon before MDT; nonrandomised before/after comparison vs retrospective cohort n=806.

title: Inflammatory risk and cardiovascular events in patients without obstructive coronary artery disease: the ORFAN multicentre, longitudinal cohort study
evidence: Longitudinal cohort of 40,091 consecutive CCTA patients across 8 UK NHS hospitals (nested cohort with long-term follow-up). Validates the FAI Score embedded in the AI-Risk prognostic model. Authors' reply states the study 'did not develop any new artificial intelligence (AI) model, but rather validated an existing LOCKED COMMERCIAL MEDICAL DEVICE in a new cohort'.

title: Prediction of mortality, bleeding, and ischaemic events in patients with cancer and acute coronary syndrome: a model development and validation study
evidence: 1,017,759 ACS patients: England 815,170 (36,771 with cancer), Sweden 194,059 (10,262), Switzerland 8,530 (203), Jan 2004-Aug 2023. Competing-risks machine learning, 6-month horizon, predicting all-cause mortality, major bleeding and ischaemic events from 11 clinically available variables. Externally validated in geographically distinct held-out datasets (English Midlands, Sweden, Switzerland). Internal tAUC 0.84 mortality / 0.70 bleeding / 0.79 ischaemic; external similar (mortality 0.80-0.84).
